written.myAnswer: Strong, unique passwords are harder to guess and help prevent unauthorized access to your accounts.
Software updates often include security fixes that protect devices from new threats.
Avoid clicking unknown links or downloading files from untrusted sources.
2FA requires an additional verification step after the password, making unauthorized account access more difficult.
Public Wi-Fi networks are often less secure, so avoid using them for sensitive transactions.
Be cautious of unsolicited requests for personal information and verify the sender through a trusted method before responding.
Carefully limit what you share, especially personal details such as your address, phone number, or school name, to protect your privacy.
Do not provide the information; verify the sender and request through a trusted source first.

Use strong, unique passwords and 2FA; keep software updated; avoid unknown links and untrusted downloads; set privacy controls and limit personal information shared; avoid sensitive transactions on public Wi-Fi; watch for scams; review account activity; and back up important data.
